niche.habitat: Jet stream boundaries (0.5–2 bar, ammonia/water cloud decks)
niche.diet: Cloud plankton, small floaters, chemotrophic aerosols

body: Flattened carapace, lateral walking legs, tucked ventral gas-bladder, asymmetrical raptorial chelae, hydrodynamic leading edge

links: Minimizes frontal drag in thin air
Distributes hydrostatic pressure evenly during migration
Prevents tissue collapse across steep pressure gradient

skill.effect: Negates 60% vertical shear damage when anchored to ice-hail.

journal.en: They ride the fall like a kite.

plausibility.summary: A dorsoventrally compressed body lowers projected area and skin friction in a fast, dusty ammonia–water cloud deck, spreading depth-related mechanical load over a broad ventral surface—consistent with F3 (high effective weight), F9 (steep pressure–altitude gradient), and F20 (pressure matching). Anchoring the flat profile to dense ammonia ice hail near ~0.7 bar (F6) is a credible way to resist vertical shear without constant swimming.

temperament: Skittish, territorial, ritualistic, herd-coordinated via infrasound
secrets: Their carapace mineralizes with ammonium hydrosulfide crystals that conduct low-frequency infrasound, effectively turning their entire body into a parabolic receiver.
During the brief ammonia rain, they molt in synchronized swarms; the fresh shells are highly prized by players for crafting pressure-equalization gear.
moments: When the zonal wind drops, the swarm freezes. Thousands of flat plates align perfectly with the dim light, becoming invisible mirrors. Only the infrasonic clack of claws reminds you they are there.

journal.en: They ride the fall like a kite.
Earth's crust forced crabs into a mold; here, the sky itself became the anvil. A textbook case of carcinisation, except the anvil is wind, the forge is pressure, and the crab is flying.
